chunks: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Hammad ibn Isa and Fadala and Safwan, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who visited the House (Kaaba) and did not cease from his tawaf, supplication, and sa'i and supplication until the dawn broke. He said: 'There is no penalty upon him, for he was in obedience to Allah, Exalted and Glorious.' The other view is that he may have left Mina after midnight, for whenever he leaves after midnight for the visitation, no penalty is obligatory upon him, although it is preferable that he does not leave until morning, which indicates that.

key_terms.السَّعْيِ: The Sa'i (walking between Safa and Marwa)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who stays in Mecca performing worship until after dawn without leaving Mina?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for pilgrims who delay leaving Mina for the purpose of continued worship (*tawaf* and *du'a*) until after dawn, ruling that no penalty is due as the delay constitutes an act of obedience. The text further distinguishes between leaving Mina after midnight for visitation versus staying until morning, establishing the latter as the preferred (*afdal*) practice. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on intention (*niyyah*) and the flexibility of ritual timing when rooted in devotion.
